# Simulate 3D point cloud

Simulates a 3D point cloud by sampling points from a triangular mesh and
adding random measurement noise. Optionally, a floor point cloud can be
generated around the object.

## Usage

``` r
simulateCloud(mesh, n, rgen = .rtnormDefault, floor = NULL, ...)
```

## Arguments

- mesh:

  `mesh3d` object representing the surface from which points are
  sampled.

- n:

  Number of points to sample from `mesh`.

- rgen:

  Random number generator used to generate measurement noise. By
  default, a truncated normal distribution is used.

- floor:

  Optional list specifying the floor simulation parameters. It must
  contain `n`, the number of floor points, and may contain `gap` and
  `margin`. If `NULL`, no floor is generated. Default is `NULL`.

- ...:

  Additional arguments passed to `rgen`.

## Value

A numeric matrix with three columns (`X`, `Y`, `Z`) containing the
simulated point cloud.

## Details

Points are sampled from `mesh` using
[`sampleMesh()`](https://modes-cemi.github.io/dimControl/reference/sampleMesh.md)
and independently perturbed in the X, Y and Z directions using random
values generated by `rgen`.

By default, the measurement noise follows a truncated normal
distribution with mean 0, standard deviation 0.2, and lower and upper
bounds of -0.5 and 0.5, respectively.

If `floor` is not `NULL`, a floor point cloud is generated using
[`simulateFloor()`](https://modes-cemi.github.io/dimControl/reference/simulateFloor.md).
The list element `n` specifies the number of floor points. If `gap` or
`margin` are not supplied, values of 2 and 20, respectively, are used.

The same random number generator and additional parameters supplied
through `...` are used for the object and floor.

## Examples

``` r
library(rgl)

data("cad", package = "dimControl")

data <- simulateCloud(mesh = cad, n = 1e5, floor = list(n = 5e3, gap = 2,
                      margin = 20))
head(data)
#>             X         Y            Z
#> [1,] 332.3466 305.42619  0.027891868
#> [2,] 142.4145 220.92719 -0.219554056
#> [3,] 314.4968 440.92718  0.401965850
#> [4,] 109.3850 110.33467 -0.002297838
#> [5,] 374.2672  34.85208 -0.110053806
#> [6,] 492.5494   7.19970  0.200904595

# Represent the simulated point cloud
open3d() # Alternatively, use `legendplot::new3d()` to clear the current device or open a new one
points3d(data, col = "gray")
```
